finding.claim: /fetch2 only checks that the URL scheme is http/https, then fetches it with redirects enabled. There is no host or IP filtering, so an attacker can reach loopback, internal services and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254).
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) (views.py:22), and the first 200 chars of the body are returned to the caller

trace.note: url taken from the query string
is_http_url only tests urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https)
requests.get(url) with default allow_redirects=True; response body is reflected

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url checks the scheme only, with no host, IP or port restriction. Redirects are followed. There is no network-level egress control in the code.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is scheme-only; the stronger is_safe_url is used only on /fetch, not /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 takes the url query parameter, passes it only through the scheme-only check at validators.py:7, then calls requests.get(url) with redirects enabled and returns the first 200 chars of the body, so internal hosts and 169.254.169.254 are reachable.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the URL with is_safe_url, which resolves the hostname via getaddrinfo, and then requests.get resolves it again. This is a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU: an attacker-controlled DNS name with a short TTL can return a public IP for the check and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 for the fetch. is_safe_url also checks only the first-resolved port (parsed.port or 443), and requests may use a different port or an alternate IP form.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5, allow_redirects=False) (views.py:14), with the body reflected

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo resolves the hostname once for checking
private, loopback, link-local and reserved IPs are rejected
requests.get(url) resolves the hostname again and connects, with no pinning of the checked IP

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allow-list, resolved-IP private/loopback/link-local/reserved check, and allow_redirects=False (redirect bypass is closed). The checked IP is not the one connected to, and nothing is enforced at connect time. ip.is_global is not used. The exploit needs a DNS rebinding setup, so this is lower confidence than finding 1.

verdict.guard_found: is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18): scheme allow-list plus resolved-IP private/loopback/link-local/reserved check, with allow_redirects=False; no host allow-list and no IP pinning at connect time
verdict.reason: The url from request.args (views.py:11) is resolved once in validators.py:14 and checked at validators.py:16, then requests.get at views.py:14 resolves it again without pinning, so DNS rebinding can bypass the check; this is not a closing guard.
